title: Consolidate CUDA provider profiles and lazy-symbol umbrella to reduce probe jitter
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Our inference nodes exhibit intermittent cold-start latency spikes and spurious symbol errors across mixed CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS images. Root cause analysis points to duplicate provider probing and eager soft-linking of vendor libraries during startup. This ticket consolidates per-image CUDA provider profiles into a single verified runtime profile and introduces a 'lazy-symbol umbrella' that defers non-critical library resolution until the first invocation path requires it. Goals: reduce probe jitter, minimize runtime symbol conflicts, and make CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades less disruptive to live fleets.
acceptance_criteria: Probe-time 95th percentile reduced by >=40% on cold-start experiments vs baseline (measured across mixed-GPU fleet)
No new symbol-resolution errors in canary pool during Triton 3.1 + CUTLASS 3.2 upgrade run
Upgrade path documented: per-image provider profile -> single runtime profile; rollback procedures validated
Automated compatibility test added to CI that exercises 3 CUDA versions (11.8, 12.2, 12.3) and Triton variants
Security review completed and KMS/HSM usage unchanged by packaging changes
implementation_notes: High-level plan: (1) Introduce provider-profile manifest (json) embedded in runtime image that enumerates supported CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS ABI pairs. (2) Implement a lazy-symbol umbrella loader that registers stubs for optional symbols and resolves them on first use; critical symbols (driver init, device enumeration) remain eagerly resolved. (3) Add an opt-in environment flag REDWOOD_LAZY_LINK=true for canary nodes. (4) Create a shim that normalizes vendor lib paths and removes duplicate RTLD_GLOBAL loads in startup code. (5) Instrument telemetry (probe_time_ms, symbol_resolve_count, fallback_invocations) for all stages. Trade-offs: lazy resolution reduces startup time but can surface errors later in runtime; to mitigate, we trigger a synthetic warmup invocation post-load in canary to exercise common paths. We will avoid touching user-visible APIs and keep changes confined to runtime loader layer.
testing_plan: Unit tests for umbrella loader stubbing logic and fallback paths. Integration tests in CI that build three image variants and run a small synthetic workload that exercises attention kernels, KV cache ops, and batching. Canary fleet run for 48 hours with 5% traffic and synthetic warmup traffic; monitor latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate, and fallback counts. Post-canary, run blue-green rollout for Dedicated pools with staged capacity increases (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Rollback tested via image tag revert and config toggle. Attach benchmark artifacts to PR.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature-flag. 2) Deploy to internal staging and run full CI matrix. 3) Enable REDWOOD_LAZY_LINK on 5% canary fleet for 48h; execute synthetic warmup. 4) If no regressions, expand to 25% for 24h. 5) Full rollout to runtime-1.20 images with automatic fallback to legacy loader if persistent symbol errors detected. 6) Post-rollout: run nightly compatibility matrix for 2 weeks to catch regressions from newer CUDA/CUTLASS drivers.
